abstract: Machine-learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) prioritizes promising protein variants for experimental testing, but performance depends on campaign design. We present MLDEx, a systematic benchmark of 557,143 simulated campaigns across 16 protein fitness landscapes, covering 28 representations, eight regressors, three acquisition rules, four initial training-set sizes, and four batch sizes. Going beyond previous benchmarks, MLDEx jointly evaluates these design choices and tests whether recommended configurations generalize to unseen protein landscapes. With small initial sets, ML guidance required 2.2-2.8 times fewer assays than random screening for comparable success, but this advantage diminished with larger sets. At 200 total assays, zero-shot screening achieved 56.2% success versus 44.6% for MLDE, with similar performance at larger budgets. Representation-regressor rankings varied substantially between landscapes: configurations selected on 15 landscapes performed 13.3 percentage points worse on the held-out landscape. MLDEx identifies broadly applicable campaign-design principles but cautions against transferring model rankings to new proteins.
